name: Contextual Contraction Appropriateness
description: Analyzes the sociolinguistic placement and rhythmic timing of contractions to detect awkward, algorithmically injected informality.
mechanism: While simple frequency analysis counts how often contractions appear, this method evaluates *where* and *how* they are used. Large Language Models often struggle with sociolinguistic consistency. When instructed to 'write casually' or 'be relatable', an AI might abruptly inject contractions ('don't', 'it's') into sentences that otherwise feature rigid, highly formal vocabulary and complex academic syntax, creating a jarring stylistic clash. Furthermore, human writers often instinctively spell out words ('do not') for rhythmic emphasis at the end of a clause or during a dramatic point, whereas an algorithm might blindly contract the words based on a forced parameter. This method maps the semantic formality of the surrounding sentence against the presence of the contraction. A high mismatch score indicates an algorithmic author attempting to 'synthesize' a conversational tone without genuinely understanding human emotional rhythm.
useCase: Detecting 'prompt-injected informality' in blogs, marketing copy, and synthetic social media posts where the AI awkwardly mixes textbook formality with forced casual contractions.
strengths:
• Highly resilient against advanced prompting (e.g., 'use contractions to sound human'), because the AI usually fails to match the contraction to the appropriate sentence rhythm or vocabulary tier.
• Captures the 'uncanny valley' feeling of corporate AI text trying too hard to be friendly.
• Acts as a powerful semantic amplifier when combined with readability and lexical density metrics.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when evaluating humans who are non-native speakers or inexperienced writers attempting to adopt a 'professional yet friendly' tone.
• Completely inapplicable to languages without syntactic verbal contractions (e.g., Chinese, Japanese, Korean).
• Requires significant context around the contraction to establish the baseline stylistic tone of the sentence.
parameters:
Analysis: Stylistic Clash Mapping & Contextual Rhythm
Metric: Sociolinguistic Formality vs. Contraction Placement
Output: 0-100 Stylistic Dissonance (Forced Informality) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-75%. Highly specialized. Excels at identifying AI struggling to maintain a consistent 'persona', but requires sufficient text length to establish a baseline.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
